patch_description: Fuses the velocity-clamping idea (Gen 41, which delivered the cluster's best smoothness 0.56 and fewest false reversals) into the two-pass Kalman/RTS core (Gen 37, superior noise reduction). After the second RTS refinement pass and before the zero-phase bilateral damper, per-step displacement is clamped using the smoothed velocity state: |y[k]−y[k−1]| ≤ 2·|xs[k,1]| + slack·σ_r. The clamp is applied in a forward sweep plus a mirrored backward sweep so it remains zero-phase (net lag-free). A guard checks correlation between clamped and unclamped signals; if corr < 0.97 the slack doubles progressively (up to effectively disabling) to preserve tracking fidelity. The clamp eliminates noise-induced overshoots in per-step displacement — the dominant source of spurious slope changes and false reversals — without flattening genuine fast dynamics, since genuine moves are accompanied by large velocity states and are never clamped.
